title: llm-prd-idea-parking-lot-aisha-khan
content:
Context:
- Quick parking lot / rough PRD outline for routing + caching features tied to hosted API performance goals.
- Notes to self mostly; will distill into proper PRD once we sync with SRE + runtime infra.

Problem statement:
- Customers see variable latency/cost for similar workloads. Some variance due to model variant routing, cold KV cache misses, and suboptimal batching for short prompt workloads.
- Need lightweight product controls to:
  * route requests by latency/cost/quality policy,
  * expose caching controls (prefix caching, TTLs),
  * allow app teams to opt-in to fallback models for availability/cost.

Goals (high level):
- Reduce P95 latency for typical chat workloads by 15% for paid hosted tier (target: drop from 420ms -> ~360ms).
- Reduce per-token cost for short-turn conversations by 10% via smarter routing + caching.
- Provide safe defaults so PLG users see benefits with minimal config.

Non-goals:
- Full rewrite of batching engine (infra-own).
- Replacing model catalog/selection heuristics entirely - start with additive policies.

Feature ideas (parking lot):
1) Policy-based routing config (app-level)
   - Route by: latency-SLO, cost-budget, region, model-quality tags (e.g., "high-quality", "fast-quant").
   - Simple DSL for policy priority: e.g., [latency:SLO<200ms] -> model-A; else model-B.
   - UI + API: define policy per API key/route.
   - User stories:
     * As an app dev, I want requests under my latency SLO to prefer low-latency model variants so user interactions feel snappy.
     * As a platform engineer, I want to pin critical routes to high-reliability capacity during incidents.

2) Prefix/KV cache controls exposed to users
   - Allow route-level TTL override, whitelist prefixes that can be cached, and a conservative default caching policy.
   - Expose cache-hit metrics in console and cost savings estimates.
   - User stories:
     * As an app dev, I can mark deterministic prefixes (system prompts) to be cached so repeated assistant contexts are cheaper.

3) Fallback model chaining and weighted fallback
   - On capacity pressure or timeouts, route to preconfigured fallback variants (e.g., quantized or smaller models).
   - Weighted fallback allows mixing for quality (e.g., 80% fast model, 20% high-quality) for A/B style tradeoffs.

4) Auto-suggest optimizations in Console (guided recommendations)
   - Analyze routes and suggest policy/caching based on traffic patterns (e.g., many short prompts -> enable short-turn batching config).

5) Developer quickstart and sample configs
   - Catalog of policy recipes: low-latency chat, low-cost embed pipeline, availability-first for enterprise.

Rough product surface (API + Console):
- API: POST /policies -> create policy, attach to route. Simple JSON schema (name, priority, matchers, actions).
- Console: per-route policy editor, cache controls, simulated impact estimate (latency & cost).

Metrics (how we measure success):
- Per-route P50/P95 latency (before/after baseline).
- Per-token cost delta for effected routes.
- Cache hit ratio (route-level).
- Number of customers adopting default policy vs custom.
- Impact on error rate when using fallback chaining.

Open questions / risks:
- How much control should we expose vs safest defaults? (security / correctness concerns if caching user content).
- Data residency / privacy: caching user prompts must respect PII/enterprise compliance. Need integration with private deployments KMS and retention settings.
- Runtime constraints: what policy evaluation throughput can router handle? Need SRE perf estimates.
- UX complexity: risk of overwhelming PLG devs with policy DSL.

Next steps (short-term):
- Sync with SRE + serving-runtime (Zoe, Raja) to get feasibility on policy eval perf and cache eviction hooks (owner: Aisha). due: 2026-02-05 (tentative).
- Draft API schema for policies and minimal console mockups (owner: Aisha).
- Create measurement plan (metrics, A/B test design).

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Pull existing traffic telemetry for short-turn chat vs long-form to estimate impact. (Query: prod-metrics -> route.token_length_hist).
- Check security/compliance with privacy team re: caching prompts (ticket: SEC-498).
- Add example policy snippets here once API schema done.

Quick example policy (very rough):
{
  "name": "low-latency-chat",
  "match": {"route": "/v1/chat/*"},
  "priority": 10,
  "conditions": [{"type":"latency_slo","value":200}],
  "actions": [{"type":"route_to","model":"gptx-fast-quant"},{"type":"cache_prefix","ttl_s":3600}]
}

Rough timeline:
- Week 0-2: feasibility + infra sync, collect telemetry.
- Week 3-5: API schema + console mocks + internal RFC.
- Week 6-10: prototype policy eval + demo using one route.
- Week 11-14: pilot with 2 PLG customers + measure.

References / links:
- CONFLUENCE: INF-serve-routing-v1 (notes from runtime team)
- JIRA: PRO-1458 (customer request: "reduce latency variance")
- Slack: #runtime-ops thread "policy-routing-ideas"

Random brain dump / ideas to revisit:
- Could we allow user-specified "quality fingerprints" on responses and have routing consult real-time quality signals? probably complex.
- Consider lightweight ML model to predict whether a request will be short vs long and route accordingly.

-- end of parking-lot --

(Will convert to RFC once infra says policy eval overhead acceptable.)
